why: The statement is a pointer to the open problems of the Map folding article: the stamp-folding count t(n) (closed form or polynomial algorithm), general map-folding counts, and the complexity of folding/flat-folding maps. No in-window event touches these. Hull et al. and Fofonov count foldings for a fixed mountain-valley assignment, which the papers themselves frame as a different question from the unrestricted count: variant. The Liu et al. Gray-code listing answers a Sawada-Li listing question that the article does not name, and its core claim dates to June 2023 anyway: variant both times. Hogan's two new OEIS terms are finite instances. Eppstein's FPT flat-folding algorithm restates map folding as open and gives no polynomial algorithm: none. Arkin et al. (2000) is the long-known simple-fold result; the article's open question concerns flat-foldability beyond that, so variant. Uehara's exponential bounds on t(n) are a pre-snapshot bound. The Hogan repository has AI-adjacent traces but no system credited with mathematics, so its ai_role is none.
doubts: The researcher read the live Wikipedia article rather than the 26 January 2024 revision, so the list of open questions under the bullet is not confirmed. Arkin et al. could be read as a pre-snapshot case of the flat-foldability question if the article meant simple folds; that would not change the outcome. Verification for the old papers rests on journal publication reported by the record, and some of those journal pages were not opened.
